title: Editor Plugin SDK Lab Manifest (VS Code + JetBrains) - Draft
content:
Purpose and scope:
This working doc describes a lightweight lab to validate editor-first SDK workflows: a VS Code/JetBrains plugin prototype that exposes Redwood inference for fast feedback loops inside an editor (prompt authoring, completion preview, streaming, and local test harness). Goal is to prove a low-friction path for product engineers and extension authors to embed Redwood capabilities into dev tools with minimal infra and resilient fallbacks.

Why this experiment?
- Many teams start by building prompts in an editor or playground; capturing that flow reduces iteration time and surfaces UX friction early.
- Editor integrations act as discoverability channels for SDK primitives (streaming, tool-calls, structured output).
- We expect new patterns (prefetching suggestions, inline completions with local caching) to reduce token spend during early prototyping.

Primary outcomes (MVP acceptance):
1) Installable VS Code extension (packaged .vsix) that can: authenticate via API key/env var, render streaming completions in an editor pane, call a simple rerank/embeddings endpoint, and persist a prompt history locally.
2) Same core behavior via a JetBrains plugin prototype (basic IntelliJ run configuration) showing shallow parity for UI/behavior.
3) A tiny local test harness (node/python) that simulates poor network/fallback to cached responses and records telemetry events.
4) Runbook documenting developer-facing errors and remediation patterns.

Audience:
- Product/feature engineers who iterate on prompts and few-shot examples.
- SDK maintainers and extension authors who want a pattern to follow.
- Solutions engineers demonstrating quick demos for customers.

Non-goals (for MVP):
- Full extension marketplace packaging and billing UX.
- Enterprise SSO or HSM KMS flows.
- Deep code actions or AST-level transformations.

High-level architecture:
- Extension frontend (TS): UI, prompt editor, streaming output pane, settings (model, temperature, max_tokens).
- Local agent/harness (Node) optionally run in background for caching and offline stub responses.
- Calls to Redwood Hosted API with optional local caching layer (filesystem-based) and a small in-memory prefix cache.
- Telemetry uploader that batches events and is opt-out by default.

Quick manual prototyping steps (dev loop - shoot for 5–10 minute local demo):
1) Clone repo: git clone git@github.com:redwood-inference/editor-sdk-lab.git
2) npm install && npm run build:extension
3) Create file ~/.redwood-dev-key with a test API key or set REDWOOD_API_KEY env var
4) In VS Code, run `Extension: Run Extension` (launches Extension Development Host)
5) Open command palette -> "Redwood: Start Prompt Session" -> type prompt -> see streaming tokens appear in a side panel
6) Toggle "Offline mode" in extension settings to exercise cache/fallback responses

Minimal example: (Type-level sketch for README)
- Settings:
  - redwood.host = https://api.redwood.ai
  - redwood.model = rwd-code-lite-v1
  - redwood.apiKey = ${env}
- Example call (pseudo-TS):
  const resp = await redwood.client.generate({prompt, model, stream: true});
  resp.on('token', token => editor.append(token));

Telemetry events (MVP):
- session.start (anonymous session id)
- prompt.submit (length, model, mode: live|offline)
- fallback.cache_hit|cache_miss
- error.http_4xx|http_5xx|parse_error
Retention: batch to local file and upload on idle (user opt-out toggle). Keep no PII by default; redact file paths.

Resilience/fallback strategies:
- If network latency > 800ms on first token, show Inline spinner + optimistic cached suggestion derived from last N prompts.
- If API returns 5xx, auto-fallback to a tiny local stub (pre-baked canned responses) and tag response with a warning banner.
- Use streaming keepalive pings and a reconnect policy with exponential backoff (max 5 attempts).

Local test harness behaviours to validate:
- Simulate token drop (cut connection mid-stream) and ensure UI shows partial completion and an explicit recovery CTA ("Retry remaining tokens").
- Exercise high-latency conditions (500–1500ms token spacing) to validate UX.
- Validate cache correctness: repeated identical prompt -> cache_hit and no billing-triggering call (instrument with mocked billing endpoint).

Developer ergonomics and DX checks (quick checklist):
- Minimal setup: 3 commands to get running (clone, install, run)
- Clear error messaging (map API errors -> human-friendly prompts)
- Easy key rotation (pick up env var change without restart)
- Low-privilege telemetry (defaults off)
- Extension settings mirror Redwood Console options (model, routing policy tag, region) for parity testing

Testing matrix (what to run during lab):
- Platforms: Mac (arm/x64), Linux, Windows (WSL)
- Editors: VS Code stable + Insiders, JetBrains IDEA Community (basic flows)
- Modes: online/online-high-latency/offline
- Models: small (rwd-lite), medium (rwd-mix), streaming vs non-streaming

Acceptance criteria for internal demo (week 1):
- Installable VS Code .vsix that shows streaming completion for a 40-token prompt under normal network conditions (<300ms to first token).
- Cache fallback kicks in and provides visible annotation that data was from cache.
- Telemetry events appear in a local log and match schema.

Roadmap beyond MVP (ideas to capture):
- Save & share prompt snippets to Redwood Console (proto sync w/ user token)
- Inline code action suggestions using embeddings + reranker (requires backend support)
- Lightweight “record session” feature that captures prompt -> response -> chosen output for repro/debug/evals
- Marketplace-ready packaging and enterprise policies (per org key fetching, SSO)

Open questions / TODOs:
- Should telem use hashed user id or fully anonymous sessions? (privacy -> prefer anonymous + opt-in hashed id)
- How to surface per-token cost on the extension without exposing billing? (show estimated token count and rough USD estimate)
- JetBrains plugin parity: what is the MVP surface we can actually accomplish in 2 weeks?
- Local stub library: curate ~30 canned responses for common demo prompts (who curates?)

Docs & handoff checklist (for productizer/solutions):
- Short README for non-dev demos (1 page) with screenshots and flow description
- Troubleshooting page: common error codes and steps (API key not found, rate-limited, stream interrupted)
- Contributing guide for extension authors: code style, tests, telemetry schema
- Perf benchmarks: first-token latency across models/regions (attach CSV in repo)

Quick notes for SDK maintainers (implementation constraints):
- Avoid heavy runtime dependencies in plugin bundle (keep payload < 1.5MB ideally)
- Export a tiny runtime shim in SDK for editor envs (no DOM, no window global assumptions)
- Provide a mock client that can be swapped in for offline development (documented in README)

Links & references:
- GitHub proto PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-editor-protos/pull/42
- Jira for lab tracking: REDW-3121
- Related Confluence sketch: confluence:Editor-SDK-Onramp-Notes-2025

Short next actions (this sprint):
- [Aisha] build initial VS Code streaming pane + demo (this week)
- [Marco] prototype local cache layer + stub responses (2d)
- [Sophie] draft README & privacy draft for telemetry (3d)
- [Liam] smoke test on Windows/WSL (end of week)

Notes to self: keep this doc intentionally light and concrete — the goal is to ship something hookable for SEs and solutions folks. Leave room for design iteration but lock the installation & auth story early.

-- end of lab manifest draft --
